picks.rationale: The New York Yankees are starting Cam Schlittler, who boasts a strong 2.26 ERA and 0.95 WHIP with elite strikeout numbers, while Braves starter Grant Holmes has also been effective recently with a 2.52 ERA over his last eight appearances. The Yankees are significantly hampered offensively by the absence of Aaron Judge, Cody Bellinger, and Giancarlo Stanton, which impacts their run production. Furthermore, the Yankees have a strong tendency to hit the UNDER, doing so in 55.8% of their games in 2026.

They are looking to complete a sweep against the Seattle Mariners, who have dropped three straight games and are 3-7 over their last ten. While the Rays' starting pitcher for today is unannounced, their bullpen demonstrated strong performance in Saturday's 3-2 victory after a late scratch. In contrast, Mariners starter Emerson Hancock has struggled, losing his past two starts and failing to secure a win in his last four outings.

Conversely, the Giants are on a 4-game losing streak specifically against the Tigers. Historically, the Tigers hold a slight edge in the all-time regular season head-to-head record against the Giants (17-14). This combination of recent form and historical dominance in this specific matchup provides a strong advantage for the Tigers.

The Chicago Cubs (68-50) are a significantly stronger team this season compared to the Kansas City Royals (49-69). The Cubs also maintain a favorable all-time head-to-head record against the Royals, winning 22 of their 40 matchups (55.0%). While the Royals secured a win in their last meeting in July 2025, the Cubs' overall superior season performance and historical advantage make them a strong candidate to win by more than one run in this contest.

New York Yankees pitcher Cam Schlittler is confirmed active and starting today, and has demonstrated elite strikeout capabilities this season, with an impressive 11.02 strikeouts per nine innings and a 30.8% strikeout rate. He has accumulated 171 strikeouts in 139 2/3 innings over 24 starts, averaging nearly 5.9 innings per outing. The Braves, despite their power, exhibit a 33.5% chase rate, ranking 28th in the league, indicating a lack of plate discipline that Schlittler can exploit with his 37.6% chase rate and ability to expand the strike zone.
